svg.text: Staying close to upstream without merge access
Not needed on day one or day one hundred — but the discipline that makes it possible is free if adopted from the first commit.
haiku-os/haiku
Moves fast, mostly in areas
we never touch. Reaches our
tree only through periodic
merges of a pinned commit.
Overlap analyser
Intersect the files upstream
changed with the files we have
changed. That intersection is
the entire risk surface.
Disjoint — merge on green CI
The overwhelming majority. Build both sparc and x86_64,
merge unattended, no human in the loop.
Overlapping — stop and open an issue
A human reads it. git rerere replays resolutions we have
already made, so the same conflict is only paid for once.
KevinAdams05/HaikuSparc — the shape of our diff decides how painful all of the above is
Class A — inside */arch/sparc/*
The trap table, the TSB, context switch, the timer.
Upstream touches these paths only during tree-wide
sweeps, so conflicts are rare and shallow.
Target: 95% of our commits land here.
These are also the commits worth sending to Gerrit.
Class B — shared, cross-architecture files
The #19597 address-space split is the big one: it
changes IS_USER_ADDRESS and user_memcpy for everyone.
Every such change goes in its own labelled commit and
into a ledger explaining why it exists.
Keep this list short enough to read in one sitting.
The real answer to drift is to shrink the diff, not to merge it faster
SPARC is an official Tier-2 Haiku target with no active maintainer. Arch-specific work is exactly what upstream would accept through
review.haiku-os.org — and anything accepted upstream is a patch we no longer carry, no longer merge, and no longer have to defend.
The fork then holds only what is genuinely experimental, which is the state in which a long-lived fork stays cheap.
submit Class A upstream
Sequencing: fork hygiene and rerere from commit one · pinned-upstream bumps monthly while the kernel is unstable · automate the merge only once
the tree builds reliably, since a merge robot with no CI to gate it is just a faster way to break the build.
